## Update: the eleventh run landed, and it is the new worst case

`rb-spree-tax-provider-interface` (adjudicated 2026-09-15, Fleiss κ 0.851, zero contested)
emitted **25 findings that reduce to 15 distinct issues — +67%**, exceeding the `ts-carbon`
+50% cited above. `same_arm_merges` = 11, across **8 duplicate groups**, three of them
three-member.

Revised totals across all **11** four-arm runs: **164 emitted → 137 distinct, +19.7%** (was
+13.9% over 10 runs).

### The spree groups

| issue | rebar members (id / criteria / band) |
|---|---|
| 1.1 | `fe9362212ee777e1b` [E1,COH] blocking · `fe4973736fd1cec19` [E3] advisory |
| 2.1 | `f4bd59683171f9ef2` [E4] blocking · `fee2ecdefb4a472fd` [G1G2] blocking |
| 4.1 | `f808aa9b1ff1a1a44` [G1G2] blocking · `f9787d46f01fa1024` [G6] blocking |
| 6.1 | `fd2ab9187e0f1af59` [E1,E6] · `f867ddb18c92babcc` [T2] · `f733d5b9d1c96f596` [E5] |
| 11.1 | `fb6f563673ec04b82` [A1] · `f5bfe8629b7309691` [E4] |
| 12.1 | `fa97557f732cede1d` [T4] · `f9a1fafd8662260f0` [T11] · `f1cb101798e624148` [T11] |
| 16.1 | `fdac6206d2c64d0d5` [T5a] · `fb617713d8f0ac36b` [T5b] |
| 23.1 | `fbcd188a4af1f9c5c` [G6] · `f88e7e6caacfdf7a1` [E4] |

Group 12.1 is notable: **two of its three members carry the SAME criterion, `T11`** — so the
pattern is not only cross-criterion. The `G1G2`/`G6` shape still recurs (groups 2.1, 4.1, 23.1).

### Correction to "fingerprints do not match": one genuine id collision exists, and it is not a duplicate

Ballot items `2.1` and `2.2` both carry finding id `f4bd59683171f9ef2`. That is **one** finding
the ballot builder split into two parts, not two findings colliding — so it does not contradict
the finding above. Stated explicitly because a reader scanning ids would otherwise read it as a
counterexample. Every genuine duplicate pair in all 11 runs still has **distinct** ids.

### Drop reasons: two more, still no deduplication

The `rfi` verdict's 7 drops were all `veto:cited-reference-inaccurate`. The `spree` verdict also
has 7 drops, under **two different reasons — `low-validity` and `veto:absence-refuted`**. So
across the two sampled verdicts there are three distinct drop reasons and **none of them is
deduplication**. The drop mechanism exists and fires; it just never fires for this.

### Blocking

6 of the 19 member findings in spree's duplicate groups carry `decision=block`, including two
groups (2.1 and 4.1) blocking on **every** member. Consistent with the pattern already recorded.

### Divergent blocking eligibility within one issue — more instances

Group 1.1: `blocking_enabled=true, threshold=0.6` against `blocking_enabled=false,
threshold=0.95`. Group 11.1 and 23.1 show the same split. One issue, two different answers to
"can this block?".
